reasoning_trace.value: The paper presents a system model for an electromagnetic field exposure-aware AI framework for integrated sensing and communications-enabled ambient backscatter wireless networks. The system consists of a cellular network with a single cell, multiple user proximity wireless devices (UPWDs), and a base station (BS). The UPWDs communicate with the BS using ambient backscatter communication (ABC) and power-domain non-orthogonal multiple access (PD-NOMA). The system aims to minimize the electromagnetic field (EMF) exposure during uplink transmissions while ensuring quality of service (QoS) requirements.

reasoning_trace.value: The system uses a k-medoids clustering approach to group UPWDs into clusters, and then assigns a subcarrier to each cluster. The power allocation is done using a water-filling algorithm, which takes into account the channel gain and interference for each user in the cluster. The system also uses successive interference cancellation (SIC) to decode the received signal at the BS. The ISAC coupling mode is achieved through the use of ABC, which enables the UPWDs to reflect the RF signals and modulate them to carry information.
